title: Loh: complete scholarly reading, diplomatic-control evidence and two bounded primary checks

work.author: Dylan M. H. Loh
work.title: Diplomatic Control, Foreign Policy, and Change under Xi Jinping: A Field-Theoretic Account
work.reading_status: Complete article, footnotes, table, figure and bibliography read
work.pagination_formula: Article physical page = printed page minus 109.

visual_checks.object: Article identity, receipt and acceptance dates
Figure 1 complete concentric hierarchy and express ideal-type qualification
Exact disputed ASEAN wording and surrounding resistance account

publication_chronology.issue_designation: 2018, confirmed by PDF cover/article and publisher landing page
publication_chronology.metadata_note: File metadata dates are not a verified online release date. Article includes 2019 references/access dates and a November 2018 interview. Do not treat issue year as exact evidence cutoff.

work.rights: Cover states Creative Commons Attribution-No Derivative Works 3.0. Original PDF and renders retained outside Git; original critical memo and metadata only in repository.

method.methods_locator: Printed pp.112–113; interview entries pp.139–140; Geng entry p.142.
method.observation: Singapore think-tank employment 2013–2015, including Track II/1.5 meetings; CFAU conferences and MFA visits in Beijing 2016–2017.
method.count_boundary: Eighteen anonymous codes; Anonymous 1 lists two dates. Do not equate coded persons with a independently verified count of interview sessions. Named Geng communication is separately cited.
replication_limits: No full interview transcripts or questionnaire supplied.
No systematic pre-Xi comparison sample, recruitment/refusal accounting or reported coding protocol.
Foreign counterparts triangulate contact experience but are not independent witnesses to all Chinese instructions.
Two informants labeled North American; national identity cannot be narrowed to United States.

claim_audit.evidence: Anonymous 3, an unsuccessful applicant, reports increasing weight of loyalty under Xi; Anonymous 4 corroborates its importance. Anonymous 2 describes disagreement before a settled decision and discipline afterward.
claim_audit.limits: Interview-grounded mechanism and perceived change. Corroborating the criterion does not independently measure the historical increase. No promotion or applicant dataset.

claim_audit.evidence: Anonymous 10 describes a more restrictive atmosphere; Anonymous 9 and 6 support accompanied meetings; author observation and Anonymous 8 dinner anecdote add concrete experiences.
claim_audit.limits: No personnel regulation or enactment date supplied. Accompanied meetings are not established as a Xi-era invention; do not generalize personal-travel statement into a universal verified legal rule.

claim_audit.evidence: Anonymous 16 recalls personal social access in New York in 1998.
claim_audit.limits: Retrospective comparison across location, time, personal relationships and career stage; not a matched before/after design.

claim_audit.evidence: Author observes increasing Xi attribution in meetings 2012–2017; senior diplomatic praise and MFA-associated books supply public expressions.
claim_audit.limits: No direct link from each expression to a personnel reward, genuine belief or individual operational instruction. Author explicitly avoids saying lack of loyalty caused purges.

claim_audit.evidence: Author allows internal disagreement and says increased control can coexist with more proactive MFA activity; secondary actors retain relatively more room to speak.
claim_audit.limits: Do not convert discipline into absence of initiative or unknown concession flexibility.

claim_audit.evidence: Author reports 2013 Taiwan booklet incident and subsequent rule changes; later Chinese interviewees distinguish manner, substance and host-organization constraints.
claim_audit.limits: Organization and original/revised rules not identified. No explicit Xi mandate documented. Political representation is not equivalent to trade concession.

claim_audit.evidence: Mixed original interviews and published reporting on 2012 and 2016 meetings, with resistance by ASEAN participants.
claim_audit.limits: July 2012 example predates Xi taking the top Party post. Chinese institutional change not isolated from member preferences, power or dispute substance.

claim_audit.evidence: Article says all South China Sea references were removed from ASEAN chairman/ministerial statements in 2016 and 2017.
claim_audit.limits: Literal claim contradicted by primary checks LOH-P01 and LOH-P02. A weaker claim about contested or softened wording requires its own specified text comparison.

claim_audit.evidence: Named media reports supply most public-event description; Anonymous 18 disputes interference and frames railway dispute as bargaining.
claim_audit.limits: Not all eyewitness evidence; election/project chronology does not prove reaction to ambassador conduct. Underlying reports and subsequent rail renegotiation not independently audited here.

claim_audit.evidence: East Asian diplomat Anonymous 14 supplies interpretation of reluctance to deliver bad news.
claim_audit.limits: Not traced evidence of withheld report, Xi knowledge or an actual negotiating decision.

claim_audit.evidence: Table 1 and Figure 1 place primary/secondary actors in an idealized influence hierarchy.
claim_audit.limits: Author expressly acknowledges approximation, grouping and temporal limits. Not a verified legal organization chart or a 2026 personnel roster.

primary_checks.title: Joint Communiqué of the 49th ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meeting
primary_checks.read_scope: Opening event/date metadata and complete South China Sea section, paragraphs 174–181, printed/physical pp.29–30. Page 29 visually inspected. Other body text not read in full.
primary_checks.establishes: Dedicated South China Sea section; land-reclamation concern in paragraph 174 and non-militarization in 177; literal blanket-removal claim in Loh p.136 is false.
primary_checks.limits: Does not reconstruct drafting pressure, compare every statement, or establish concessions by named actors.

primary_checks.title: Chairman’s Statement, 30th ASEAN Summit
primary_checks.read_scope: Opening event/date metadata and complete South China Sea section, paragraphs 120–121, printed/physical p.24; page 24 visually inspected. Other body text not read in full.
primary_checks.establishes: Dedicated South China Sea section, repeated references, and expressed concerns; literal blanket-removal claim in Loh p.136 is false.
primary_checks.limits: Not a complete longitudinal language or drafting study. Retained references do not disprove watering down of other specific language.

supported_uses: Attributed evidence of more restricted informal access and increased personal loyalty signaling in early Xi diplomatic work.
Mechanism under which political discipline and proactive policy defense may coexist.
Caution against treating tone, hospitality or academic access as measures of concession authority.
unsupported_uses: A causal estimate that Xi reduced all negotiators’ flexibility.
Treating a North American interviewee as an identified US official.
Assuming ASEAN or Malaysian relative-power conditions apply to US–China negotiations.
Inferring a specific presidential mandate or information blockage from public assertiveness.
Using the failed South China Sea deletion example as evidence of institutional transformation.

completion_note: One new complete scholarly work. Two selected primary-document checks. No chapter, ledger, proposition assessment or existing source register edited. Reading bibliography does not imply reading cited works.
